ns2:section.sectionText: Topic: Access to Justice > This course explores contemporary issues related to the ability of the public to access "justice." Topics include perspectives on what justice is; barriers to obtaining justice through the formal legal system; potential solutions to these barriers. These solutions include the legal frameworks and arguments for and against entitlements to legal representation; the role of lawyers as gatekeepers and facilitators; benefits and costs of providing counsel in different contexts and cases; existing and potential alternatives to law, lawyers and courts as routes to justice; race, class and gender inequalities. The course readings emphasize empirical research.
